paragraphs: Telos Corporation is a Maryland corporation headquartered in Ashburn, Virginia. Telos Corporation, together with its subsidiaries (the "Company" or "Telos" or "We"), offers technology solutions and services that empower and protect the world's most security-conscious organizations.

We deliver efficient, adaptable, and secure solutions that protect people, organizations, and information across government and industry. From cyber governance, risk and compliance ("GRC") with Xacta®, to identity and biometric solutions, secure networks, and TSA PreCheck® enrollment, we help customers stay ahead of evolving threats. Our primary customers include the U.S. federal government, large commercial organizations and international customers. Our deep domain expertise, cleared workforce, and proven technologies give us a unique position at the intersection of cybersecurity, identity, and network security. Driven by purpose and guided by our core values, we build lasting partnerships, deliver superior solutions, and help create a more secure, interconnected world.

We conduct our business through two reportable and operating segments: Security Solutions and Secure Networks. These segments enable the alignment of our strategies and objectives and provide a framework for the timely and rational allocation of resources within the line of business.
Additional information regarding our segments is presented in Note 16 – Segment Information to the consolidated financial statements at Item 8 of this Annual Report on Form 10-K.

The Security Solutions segment delivers cybersecurity, cloud, identity, and secure messaging solutions that help government and commercial customers protect critical systems, manage cyber risk, and operate securely in complex and regulated environments. This segment combines cyber GRC solutions, secure cloud services, identity and biometric technologies, and secure messaging platforms to support mission-critical requirements for government and commercial customers operating in highly regulated and security-sensitive environments.
Security Solutions represented 90.8% and 70.9% of total revenues for fiscal years 2025 and 2024, respectively.
The Security Solutions segment offers the following solutions and services:

•Xacta: Deployed at some of the world's most security-conscious organizations, Xacta is a cyber GRC automation platform designed to help its customers meet the complex challenges of managing cyber risk and security compliance by automating processes for assessment and authorization, remediation, and continuous monitoring.

Xacta is a premier platform delivering automated cyber risk management and continuous compliance processes for systems based in the cloud, on-premises, and in hybrid environments. It supports a wide-range of frameworks and regulatory content, including National Institute of Standards and Technology ("NIST") Risk Management Framework ("RMF"), the Cybersecurity Risk Management Construct for Department of War ("DoW") IT, the NIST Cybersecurity Framework, the Federal Risk and Authorization Management Program ("FedRAMP") and the DoW's Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification ("CMMC") program, across all industries with no-code customization options for tailoring content to fit the organization's needs.

Recently, Telos launched Xacta.aiTM, the artificial intelligence ("AI") capability at the core of the Xacta cyber GRC platform, dramatically reducing compliance time and effort. Xacta.ai delivers expert-level guidance and real-time insights, empowering organizations to move from reactive compliance to proactive risk management.

•Cybersecurity Services: We offer solutions and services for the full cybersecurity lifecycle, including RMF consulting services, security assessment and compliance, engineering and evaluation, operations, penetration testing, and digital forensics. With a pedigree in cybersecurity and information assurance that spans three decades, our multi-certified cybersecurity personnel provide services and solutions that deliver continuous security assurance for business, government, and public sector critical infrastructure.

•Telos Automated Message Handling System ("Telos AMHS™"): Telos AMHS is a web-based organizational message distribution and management solution for mission-critical communications; the recognized gold standard for organizational messaging in the U.S. government. Telos AMHS is used by military field operatives for critical communications on the battlefield using the Defense Information System Agency's Organizational Messaging Service and its specialized communications protocols. Telos AMHS is also used by the Intelligence Community ("IC") for timely situational awareness and assessment reporting utilizing the Director of National Intelligence's Information Transport Service, Organizational Messaging data standards and computing infrastructure. Because Telos AMHS supports timely and reliable delivery for authoritative communications, its uses include terrorist warnings, "eyes-only" messages, military execution orders, intelligence information, overflight clearances, and Emergency Action Messages for nuclear command and control. Information exchanged at this level and for these purposes requires operational requirements for time-sensitive, guaranteed delivery, precedence, high availability, and reliability.

•Telos Identity Solutions: Telos provides a portfolio of identity solutions that support secure identity verification, biometric enrollment, and trusted identity services for government and commercial customers. These solutions address requirements related to Know Your Customer ("KYC"), identity proofing, access control, insider threat mitigation, and regulatory compliance, and are deployed across large-scale environments supporting millions of identity transactions through workstations, kiosks, laptops, mobile devices, and access control systems.

Built on secure, enterprise-grade platforms certified and operational across multiple U.S. federal agencies, these offerings enable organizations to deploy modular, scalable services supporting both business-to-business and business-to-consumer identity use cases. Telos supports major digital identity programs in the U.S., including those serving the military, transportation, healthcare, law enforcement, financial services, and civil service organizations. Telos maintains key government certifications and designations, including recognition as a TSA PreCheck enrollment provider, Aviation Channeling Services provider, Federal Bureau of Investigation ("FBI") approved Channeler, and Florida Department of Law Enforcement Registered Live Scan Service Provider.

headings: Business and Operational Risks
Our business could be negatively affected by cyber or other information security threats, breaches, or other disruptions.

If our customers do not renew their contracts for our solutions and services, or subscriptions, and expand our relationships with them, our revenue could decline and our results of operations would be adversely impacted.
Federal government spending reductions, workforce changes, and policy shifts may impact our existing operations and future opportunities for new contracts.

A failure to attract, train, retain and motivate key and skilled employees, including key members of our management team, would adversely affect our ability to execute our strategy and may disrupt our operations.
Our competitive position and future profitability depend, in part, on our ability to develop new technologies.
Our financial results may fluctuate due to increasing variability in our security solutions' sales and implementation cycles.
Failure to effectively develop and execute our sales and business development capabilities will harm our ability to grow our business.
Failure to adequately protect our intellectual property, technologies and proprietary rights could harm our business, competitive position, financial condition, and results of operations.
Our earnings and profitability may vary based on the mix of our contracts and may be adversely affected by our failure to estimate and manage costs, time, and resources accurately.
Failure to deliver high-quality technical support services may adversely affect our relationships with our customers and our financial results.
Our growth depends, in part, on the success of our strategic relationship with our partner organizations.
The inability to set optimal pricing structures for our solutions and services could adversely impact our business, financial condition and results of operations.
Artificial Intelligence ("AI") is an emerging technology and we may not be successful in our AI initiatives.
We may be subject to legal proceedings, regulatory disputes and governmental inquiries that could materially harm our business, operating results, and financial condition.
Potential future acquisitions, strategic investments, partnerships, divestitures, mergers or joint ventures may subject us to significant risks, any of which could harm our business.
Public confidence in, and acceptance of, identity platforms and biometrics generally, and our solutions and services specifically, will be a key factor in our business's continued growth.
Any decline or disruption in the travel industry or general economic downturn could materially and adversely affect our business, results of operations and financial condition.
Actions that we are taking to restructure our business to improve profitability may not be as effective as anticipated.
Goodwill and intangible assets represent significant assets on our balance sheet and any impairment on these assets could negatively impact our results of operations, and shareholders' equity.
Industry, Legal and Regulatory Risks
The business environment in which we operate is highly competitive, and we may not be able to compete successfully against existing or future competitors.
The Administration's actions, such as tariffs and other changes in international trade policies, could adversely and unexpectedly impact our business.
We are subject to the seasonality of U.S. federal government spending.
paragraphs: In your evaluation of the Company and business, you should carefully consider the risks and uncertainties as described below, together with the information included elsewhere in this Annual Report on Form 10-K and other documents we file with the SEC. These factors, as well as additional risks and uncertainties not currently known to us or that we currently believe are immaterial, may currently have, or may have, a significant impact on our business, operating results or financial condition. Actual results could differ materially from those projected in the forward-looking statements contained in this Annual Report on Form 10-K as a result of the risk factors discussed below and elsewhere in this Annual Report on Form 10-K.

We routinely experience cybersecurity threats, threats to our information technology infrastructure and attempts to gain access to our sensitive information, as do our customers, suppliers, prime and subcontractors, and strategic partners. We experience similar security threats at customer sites that we operate and manage as a contractual requirement. The threats we face vary from attacks common to most industries to more advanced and persistent, highly organized adversaries who target us because we protect national security information. While we have security measures in place to protect our data and the data of our customers or end-users of our services, our services and underlying infrastructure may in the future be materially breached or compromised as a result of the following:

•Third-party attempts to fraudulently induce employees, contractors or customers into disclosing sensitive information such as user names, passwords or other information to gain access to our customers' data, our data or our IT systems;
•Efforts by individuals or groups of hackers and sophisticated organizations, including state-sponsored organizations or nation-states;
•Cyberattacks on our internally built infrastructure; •Vulnerabilities resulting from enhancements and updates to our existing solutions;
•Vulnerabilities in the products or components across the broad ecosystem that our services operate in or are dependent on;

paragraphs: The following discussion and analysis of our financial condition and results of operations should be read in conjunction with our consolidated financial statements and the related notes to consolidated financial statements included in Part II, Item 8 of this Annual Report on Form 10-K ("10-K"). In addition to historical financial information, the following discussion and analysis contain forward-looking statements that involve risks, uncertainties and assumptions. Our actual results and timing of selected events in future periods may differ materially from those anticipated or implied in these forward-looking statements as a result of many factors, including those discussed under Item 1A, "Risk Factors," and elsewhere in this 10-K. See also "Special Note Regarding Forward-Looking Statements" at the beginning of this 10-K.
In this section, we discuss our financial condition, changes in financial condition and results of operations for the year ended December 31, 2025, compared to the year ended December 31, 2024.

For an overview of our business, including our business segments and a discussion of the services and products we provide, see Item 1, "Business" in Part I and Note 16 – Segment Information of the notes to the consolidated financial statements contained within this 10-K.

As discussed under Item 1A, "Risk Factors," we derive a substantial portion of our revenues from contracts and subcontracts with the U.S. federal government. Our revenues are generated from a number of contract vehicle and task orders. The U.S. federal government has increasingly relied on contracts that are subject to a competitive bidding process (including BPA and IDIQ Task Orders, OTAs, and other GSA schedule solicitations), resulting in greater competition and increased pricing pressure. We expect that a majority of the business that we seek in the foreseeable future will be awarded through a competitive bidding process.

Over the past several years we have sought to diversify and improve our operating margins through the evolution of our business from an emphasis on product reselling to an advanced solutions technologies provider. Although we continue to offer resold products through our contract vehicles or our prime partners' contracts, we have focused on the transformation and growth of our software and service solutions offerings, as well as the design and delivery of our manufactured and branded technologies. We emphasize leveraging technology and innovation, specifically in cybersecurity, cloud, and identity solutions, to drive growth and ensure a secure and defendable network. We continue to invest in and develop in AI integration, enhancing automation and improving existing solutions to maintain a competitive edge.

We believe our contract portfolio reflects low to moderate financial risk due to the limited number of long-term fixed-price development contracts, thus minimizing the risk of cost overruns. Our firm-fixed-price activities consist primarily of contracts for products and services at established contract prices that are designed to be repeatable solution offerings. For 2025 and 2024, the Company's revenue derived from firm-fixed-price contracts was 73.3% and 75.3%, respectively; time-and-material contract revenue was 21.8% and 14.6%, respectively; and cost-plus contract revenue was 4.9% and 10.1%, respectively.

In fiscal year ("FY") 2025, we generated approximately 91.0% of our revenues from the U.S. federal government, either as prime contractor or a subcontractor to other contractors engaged in work for the U.S. federal government, including 58.1% of our revenue from the DoW. Accordingly, our business performance is affected by the overall level of U.S. federal government spending and the alignment of our offerings and capabilities with current and future budget priorities of the U.S. federal government.

While we view the budget environment as constructive and believe there is bipartisan support for continued investment in the areas of defense and national security, it is uncertain when (and if) in any particular government fiscal year appropriations bills will be passed. During those periods of time when appropriations bills have not been passed and signed into law, U.S. federal government agencies operate under a continuing resolution ("CR"), a temporary measure that allows the government to continue operations at prior year funding levels.

The FY2025 U.S. federal government appropriations, which ran through September 30, 2025, were determined by a full-year CR. While the Administration has submitted its FY2026 budget proposal outlining its priorities, partisan disagreements over federal spending levels, among other things, have stalled progress on the required appropriations bills. Recently, on February 3, 2026, Congress passed another full-year CR for FY2026 to end the partial government shutdown. This enacted bill provides full-year funding for several programs, including defense and national security, through September 30, 2026; and also extended homeland security funding through February 13, 2026. A partial government shutdown began on February 14, 2026 after the lawmakers and the White House failed to reach a deal on legislation to fund DHS through September 2026. The impasse affects agencies such as the Transportation Security Administration, the Federal Emergency Management Agency, U.S. Coast Guard, the Secret Service, U.S. Immigration and Custom Enforcement, and U.S. Customs and Border Protection.

Congress approved a FY2026 Defense Appropriations Bill that provides $838.7 billion in discretionary funding, including $838.5 billion in defense funding and $180 million in nondefense funding. This funding prioritizes restoring military strength, accelerating modernization, and supporting personnel through pay raises. This bill moves in parallel with the National Defense Authorization Act ("NDAA"), signed in December 2025, which authorizes up to approximately $900.6 billion for national defense.

The federal government's cybersecurity and IT spending priorities for fiscal years 2025 and 2026 present both significant opportunities and notable risks for our suite of security solutions. The FY2026 NDAA authorizes approximately $15.1 billion for DoW cyber activities, representing a 4.1% increase. The FY2026 NDAA emphasizes securing the defense industrial base, accelerating artificial intelligence ("AI") integration, and harmonizing cybersecurity requirements. This increase directly aligns with our core offerings in cyber risk management (e.g., Xacta).

Further, the FY2026 budget for AI reflects a massive strategic shift toward implementation and national dominance, particularly within the defense sector. FY26 is viewed as the year federal agencies move from experimenting with AI to adopting "agentic" AI. The FY26 budget request included a record-breaking $13.4 billion for AI and autonomy initiatives within the DoW, the largest single-year investment in the agency's history. Consistent with these initiatives, in October 2025, we launched Xacta.ai, which we believe will reduce cyber compliance timelines through AI-driven automation.

The federal government cybersecurity and AI-related initiatives continue to evolve and may be influenced by changes in Administration policy, legislative action and regulatory developments. These changes may affect funding allocations, procurement strategies and compliance expectations. While management continues to monitor the federal government's initiatives and seeks to align the Company's capabilities accordingly, there can be no assurance that the future government priorities will not impose new compliance obligations, or technological advancements that will require for additional investment or affect the Company's ability to compete for or perform under government contracts.

Aside from the uncertainty in the budgetary environment, the Administration put in place a number of Executive Orders and actions that have affected, and could continue to affect, many businesses. The Administration continuously evaluates federal agencies and existing government contracts, grants, and programs for affordability, efficiency, and alignment with U.S. federal government priorities. Further, the Administration continues ever-changing actions that increase, invoke new and/or rescind tariffs on various goods imported from various countries. Changes in international trade policies, including higher tariffs on imported goods and materials, may increase the procurement costs of certain IT hardware we use internally, on our contracts, or sell to our customers.

paragraphs: Telos Corporation 是一間位於維吉尼亞州阿什本的馬裏蘭州公司。Telos Corporation 連同其子公司（以下簡稱「本公司」或「Telos」或「我們」），提供科技解決方案與服務，以賦能並保護世界上最重視安全的組織。

我們提供高效、靈活且安全的解決方案，用以保護個人、組織與資訊，遍及政府與產業領域。從網路治理、風險與合規（「GRC」）的 Xacta®，到身分與生物特徵解決方案、安全網路與 TSA PreCheck® 註冊，我們協助客戶應對不斷演變的威脅。我們的主要客戶包括美國聯邦政府、大型商業組織與國際客戶。我們深厚的專業領域知識、經過審查的員工與經過驗證的技術，使我們在網路安全、身分認證與網路安全的交叉點上擁有獨特的優勢。我們以使命為導向，並遵循核心價值觀，建立長久的合作關係，提供優質的解決方案，並協助創造更安全、更連結的世界。
我們透過兩個應報告且營運的分部進行業務：安全解決方案與安全網路。這些分部使我們能對齊策略與目標，並提供一個框架，以在業務線內及時且合理地配置資源。
有關我們分部的額外資訊，請參閱本年度報告表 10-K 第 8 項財務報表附註 16 – 分部資訊。
安全解決方案分部提供網路安全、雲端、身分認證與安全通訊解決方案，協助政府與商業客戶保護關鍵系統、管理網路風險，並在複雜且受規範的環境中安全運作。此分部結合網路 GRC 解決方案、安全雲端服務、身分與生物特徵技術，以及安全通訊平台，以支援政府與商業客戶在高度規範且安全敏感環境中的任務關鍵需求。
安全解決方案分部在會計年度 2025 年與 2024 年分別佔總營收的 90.8% 與 70.9%。
安全解決方案分部提供的解決方案與服務如下：
•Xacta：部署於世界上最重視安全的組織之一，Xacta 是一個網路 GRC 自動化平台，設計用以協助客戶應對管理網路風險與安全合規的複雜挑戰，透過自動化評估與授權、修復與持續監測的流程。

Xacta 是一個首選平台，提供自動化網路風險管理與持續合規流程，適用於雲端、本地端及混合環境中的系統。它支援廣泛的架構與法規內容，包括國家標準技術研究院（"NIST"）風險管理架構（"RMF"）、國防部（"DoW"）資訊科技的網路安全風險管理架構、NIST 網路安全架構、聯邦風險與授權管理計畫（"FedRAMP"）以及國防部（"DoW"）的網路安全成熟度模型認證（"CMMC"）計畫，適用於所有產業，並提供無程式碼客製化選項，以符合組織的特定需求。
最近，Telos 發布了 Xacta.aiTM，這是 Xacta 網路安全 GRC 平台的核心人工智慧（"AI"）功能，大幅減少合規所需時間與努力。Xacta.ai 提供專家級的指導與即時洞察，協助組織從應對式合規轉為預防式風險管理。
•網路安全服務：我們提供完整的網路安全生命週期解決方案與服務，包括 RMF 諮詢服務、安全評估與合規、工程與評估、運作、滲透測試與數位鑑識。憑藉超過三十年的網路安全與資訊保障經驗，我們的多證書網路安全人員提供服務與解決方案，以實現企業、政府與公部門關鍵基礎設施的持續安全保證。

•Telos 自動化訊息處理系統（"Telos AMHS™"）：Telos AMHS 是一個基於網頁的組織訊息分發與管理解決方案，用於關鍵任務通訊；被認為是美國政府組織通訊的黃金標準。Telos AMHS 由軍事作戰人員在戰場上使用，透過國防資訊系統局（Defense Information System Agency）的組織通訊服務及其專用通訊協議進行關鍵通訊。Telos AMHS 也用於情報機構（"IC"）以進行即時的情況感知與評估報告，透過國家情報局（Director of National Intelligence）的資訊傳輸服務、組織通訊資料標準與計算基礎設施。由於 Telos AMHS 支援即時且可靠的權威通訊傳遞，其應用包括恐怖攻擊警告、"僅限特定人員"訊息、軍事執行命令、情報資訊、飛行許可與核子指揮與控制的緊急行動訊息。在這個層級進行這些用途的資訊交換，需要運作需求，包括時間敏感、保證傳遞、優先順序、高可用性與可靠性。
•Telos 身分解決方案：Telos 提供一系列身分解決方案，用於支援政府與商業客戶的安全身分驗證、生物特徵註冊與受信任的身分服務。這些解決方案應對與 "瞭解您的客戶"（"KYC"）、身分驗證、存取控制、內部威脅緩解與法規合規相關的需求，並部署於大規模環境中，支援數百萬筆身分交易，透過工作站、自助服務機臺、筆記型電腦、行動裝置與存取控制系統。

這些產品建立在安全、企業級平台之上，並已獲得美國多個聯邦機構的認證與運作。這些服務使組織能夠部署模組化、可擴展的服務，支援企業對企業與企業對消費者身分使用案例。Telos 支援美國主要的數位身分計畫，包括服務軍事、運輸、醫療、執法、金融服務與民用服務機構的計畫。Telos 保持關鍵政府認證與指定，包括被認可為 TSA PreCheck 註冊服務提供者、航空通關服務提供者、聯邦調查局（"FBI"）核准的通關服務提供者，以及佛羅裏達州執法部門註冊的實時掃描服務提供者。

paragraphs: 以下對我們財務狀況及營運成果的討論與分析，應與我們的合併財務報表及相關合併財務報表附註，一同閱讀，這些財務報表包含於本年度報告表 10-K（"10-K"）第二部分，第 8 項。除了歷史財務資訊外，以下討論與分析包含前瞻性陳述，這些陳述涉及風險、不確定性與假設。我們未來的實際結果及特定事件的發生時間，可能與這些前瞻性陳述所預期或暗示的結果有重大差異，這是因為許多因素，包括在第 1A 項 "風險因素" 中討論的那些因素，以及其他地方的 10-K 內容。請參閱本 10-K 開頭的 "關於前瞻性陳述的特別說明"。
在本節中，我們討論我們的財務狀況、財務狀況的變化及營運成果，比較 2025 年 12 月 31 日為結算日的年度與 2024 年 12 月 31 日為結算日的年度。
如要了解我們的業務，包括我們的業務分部及我們提供的服務與產品討論，請參閱第一部分第 1 項 "業務" 及財務報表附註中的第 16 項 "分部資訊"。
如第 1A 項 "風險因素" 所討論，我們的營業收入有相當大一部分來自與美國聯邦政府的契約及次承包契約。我們的營業收入來自多種契約類型與任務訂單。美國聯邦政府越來越依賴需經競爭性招標程序的契約（包括 BPA 和 IDIQ 任務訂單、OTAs 及其他 GSA 採購招標），這導致競爭增加及價格壓力上升。我們預期，在可預見的未來，我們尋求的業務中，大多數將透過競爭性招標程序授予。

在過去幾年中，我們致力於透過業務從強調產品經銷轉向進階解決方案科技供應商，來實現多元化與改善營運毛利。雖然我們繼續透過契約類型或我們首承包商契約提供經銷產品，但我們已著重於軟體與服務解決方案的轉型與成長，以及我們製造與品牌科技的設計與交付。我們強調運用科技與創新，特別是在網路安全、雲端與身分解決方案，以推動成長並確保網路的安全與防禦。我們持續投資與發展 AI 積合，提升自動化並改善現有解決方案，以維持競爭優勢。

我們認為，我們的契約組合反映低至中等的財務風險，這是因為長期固定價格開發契約的數量有限，因此可降低成本超支的風險。我們的固定價格活動主要為產品與服務的契約，這些契約價格已建立，並設計為可重複的解決方案。2025 年及 2024 年，本公司來自固定價格契約的營業收入分別為 73.3% 及 75.3%；時間與材料契約的營業收入分別為 21.8% 及 14.6%；成本加契約的營業收入分別為 4.9% 及 10.1%。
在會計年度（"FY"）2025 年，我們約有 91.0% 的營業收入來自美國聯邦政府，無論是以首承包商或次承包商身份，與其他承包商合作執行美國聯邦政府的工作，包括 58.1% 的營業收入來自 DoW。因此，我們的業務表現受美國聯邦政府支出總體水準及我們的產品與能力與美國聯邦政府當前及未來預算優先順序的匹配程度影響。
雖然我們認為預算環境是建設性的，並相信在防禦與國家安全領域有兩黨支持持續投資，但不確定任何特定政府財政年度是否會通過並簽署撥款法案。在撥款法案未通過並簽署為法律的期間，美國聯邦政府機構將根據持續決議（"CR"）運作，這是一項臨時措施，允許政府以前一年的資金水準繼續運作。

FY2025 美國聯邦政府預算經費，運作至 2025 年 9 月 30 日，是由全年持續撥款（CR）決定。雖然行政部門已提交 FY2026 預算提案，說明其優先事項，但因國會兩黨對聯邦支出水準的爭議，以及其他因素，已使相關預演算法案的進展停滯。最近，在 2026 年 2 月 3 日，國會通過另一項全年持續撥款（CR）法案，用以結束部分政府停擺。此經立法程序通過的法案，為多個計畫提供全年經費，包括國防與國家安全，至 2026 年 9 月 30 日為止；並同時將國土安全經費延長至 2026 年 2 月 13 日。部分政府停擺則於 2026 年 2 月 14 日開始，因立法者與白宮未能就立法達成共識，以資助國土安全部（DHS）至 2026 年 9 月。此僵局影響機構如運輸安全管理局、聯邦緊急管理署、美國海岸 guard、特別勤務組、美國移民與關稅執法局，以及美國關稅與邊境保護局。

美國聯邦政府於財政年2025及2026年的網路安全與資訊科技支出優先順序，對我們的網路安全解決方案組合而言，同時帶來重大機會與顯著風險。財政年2026的國防授權法案（NDAA）授權約15.1 十億美元用於DoW的網路活動，較前一年成長4.1%。財政年2026的國防授權法案強調確保國防工業基礎、加速人工智慧（"AI"）整合，並協調網路安全需求。此成長直接與我們在網路風險管理（例如Xacta）的核心業務相符。

此外，2026財年（FY2026）的人工智慧（AI）預算反映了一項重大的戰略轉變，朝向實施與國家主導，特別是在防禦部門。2026財年被視為聯邦機構從實驗人工智慧轉向採用「自主」人工智慧的年份。2026財年預算請求中，包含了一筆創紀錄的13.4 十億美元，用於美國國防部（DoW）內的人工智慧與自主性計畫，這是該機構歷史上單年最大的投資。與這些計畫一致，於2025年10月，我們啟動了Xacta.ai，我們認為這將透過人工智慧驅動的自動化，縮短網路合規時程。
聯邦政府的網路安全與 AI 相關計畫持續演進，可能受行政部門政策變動、立法行動與規範發展的影響。這些變動可能影響經費分配、採購策略與合規預期。雖然管理層持續監測聯邦政府的計畫，並努力使本公司能力與之對應，但無法保證未來政府優先事項不會帶來新的合規義務，或技術進步需要額外投資，或影響本公司參與政府契約的競爭能力與執行能力。
除了預算環境的不確定性，行政部門已實施多項行政命令與行動，影響，並可能持續影響，許多企業。行政部門持續評估聯邦機構與現有政府契約、補助金與計畫的可負擔性、效率與對美國聯邦政府優先事項的對應。此外，行政部門持續進行變動，提高、啟動新或廢除來自不同國家進口商品的關稅。國際貿易政策的變動，包括提高進口商品與材料的關稅，可能提高我們內部使用、契約或銷售給客戶的某些 IT 硬體的採購成本。

headings: 營運與業務風險
本公司業務可能因網路或其它資訊安全威脅、入侵或其它中斷事件而受到負面影響。
若客戶未續約本公司解決方案與服務或訂閱項目，亦未擴大與本公司之合作關係，則本公司營業收入可能下降，且營運結果將受到不利影響。
美國聯邦政府預算減縮、人力結構變動及政策改變，可能影響本公司現有營運及未來新契約之商機。
若無法吸引、培訓、留住並激勵關鍵且具專業技能之員工，包括本公司管理團隊之關鍵成員，將不利於本公司執行策略，並可能幹擾本公司營運。
本公司之競爭地位與未來獲利能力，部分取決於本公司開發新技術之能力。
本公司財務結果可能因安全解決方案銷售與實踐週期之變動性增加而產生波動。
若無法有效開發與執行銷售與業務拓展能力，將影響本公司拓展業務之能力。
未能充分保護本公司的智慧財產權、技術及專有權利，可能損害本公司的業務、競爭地位、財務狀況及營運成果。
本公司獲利與獲利能力可能因合約組成的變化而有所不同，並可能因未能準確預估及管理成本、時間與資源而受到不利影響。
未能提供高品質的技術支援服務，可能對本公司與客戶的關係及財務結果造成不利影響。
本公司成長在部分程度上依賴與合作機構的戰略關係之成功。
無法為本公司的解決方案及服務設定最佳定價結構，可能對本公司業務、財務狀況及營運成果造成不利影響。
人工智慧（"AI"）是一項新興技術，本公司可能無法成功執行本公司的AI計畫。
本公司可能面臨法律訴訟、監管爭議及政府調查，這些情況可能對本公司業務、營運成果及財務狀況造成重大損害。
未來可能的併購、戰略投資、合作夥伴關係、資產處置、合併或合作企業，可能使本公司面臨重大風險，任何一種情況都可能損害本公司業務。
民眾對身分平台及生物特徵技術的信賴與接受度，以及本公司解決方案與服務的認可，將是本公司業務持續成長的關鍵因素。
若旅遊業出現衰退或中斷，或總體經濟陷入衰退，將可能對本公司業務、營運結果與財務狀況造成重大且不利的影響。
本公司為改善獲利能力而進行的業務重整措施，可能無法達到預期的效果。
商譽及無形資產為本公司資產負債表上的重要資產，若這些資產發生減值，將可能對本公司營運結果及股東權益造成負面影響。
產業、法律與法規風險
本公司所處的業務環境競爭激烈，本公司可能無法成功對抗現有或未來的競爭對手。
美國政府的政策行動，例如關稅及其他國際貿易政策的變更，可能對本公司業務造成不利且意外的影響。
本公司受美國聯邦政府支出季節性影響。
paragraphs: 在評估本公司及其業務時，您應謹慎考慮下列所描述的風險與不確定性，並配合本年度10-K表報表及其他文件中所包含的資訊，以及我們向美國證券交易委員會（SEC）所提交的其他文件。這些因素，以及目前我們尚未知悉或目前認為不重要的其他風險與不確定性，可能目前對我們的業務、營運結果或財務狀況產生重大影響。實際結果可能與本年度10-K表報表中所包含的預測性陳述有顯著差異，原因在於下列所討論的風險因素及其他地方所提及的風險因素。

我們經常面臨網路安全威脅、資訊科技基礎設施的威脅，以及試圖取得我們敏感資訊的行為，這也發生在我們的客戶、供應商、主承包商與次承包商，以及戰略夥伴身上。我們在客戶場地所經營與管理的場所，也會面臨類似的安全威脅，這是根據契約要求所必須履行的。我們所面對的威脅，從大多數產業常見的攻擊，到更為先進且持續性的、高度組織化的對手，這些對手會針對我們，因為我們保護國家安全資訊。雖然我們已設有安全措施以保護我們的資料以及我們客戶或服務終端使用者的資料，但我們的服務與基礎設施未來仍可能因下列原因而遭受重大入侵或損害：
•第三方試圖詐欺性誘使員工、承包商或客戶揭露敏感資訊，例如使用者名稱、密碼或其他資訊，以取得客戶的資料、我們的資料或我們的資訊科技系統；
•個人或羣體駭客以及高階組織的行動，包括由國家支持的組織或國家；
•針對我們 internally built 基礎設施的網路攻擊；•因對我們現有解決方案進行升級與更新而產生的漏洞；
•在我們服務運作或依賴的廣泛生態系中，產品或零組件的漏洞；
